recorded.outcome:q-slot-without-room: Section 'A Record Pattern Never Matches null, at Any Depth; var and the Component's Declared Type Do': 'A record pattern starts with an instanceof test, and null is an instance of nothing ... That holds at every level. The address is null, so Address(var c, var pc) fails, the whole pattern fails, and book calls a payment "not a payment"' (the else/throw branch runs); output 'Payer(var id, Address(var c, var pc)): false'. Reference table: 'a record pattern R(...) | Value is null: doesn't match'. Same shape as the quiz (nested record pattern on a null component, else branch).

recorded.outcome:q-counter-type-changes: Section 'A Narrower Type on a Component Is a Test, So a Payload Whose Type Changes Stops Matching': payload declared Object, 'String json asks a question: is this component's value a String? It is not a cast, and a byte[] makes the pattern fail without a ClassCastException'; 'Wherever a chain of record patterns ends, in an else or a default...' (leftover branch). Reference: 'S x, S narrower than the declared type | doesn't match | doesn't match, no exception'. Summary: 'A payload whose type changes falls through to the leftover branch'. Integer is narrower-type-mismatch for both Long and Double, so the last branch runs.

recorded.outcome:q-stale-quote: Section 'Matching Calls the Accessors, and an Exception From One Arrives as MatchException': 'When an accessor throws during a match, the match throws MatchException with the original exception as its cause ... The catch for StringIndexOutOfBoundsException never ran, and in a batch job one bad record from an old import ends the batch.' Reference (accessor-calls table, switch context): 'any accessor throwing during a match | MatchException, cause = the accessor's exception'. The page's runnable example uses instanceof, not switch; the switch case rests on the Reference row and the Summary ('their exceptions arrive as MatchException').

recorded.outcome:q-for-header: Callout 'Where Java 21 allows them' in section 'A Record Pattern Tests the Type, Then Binds Each Component by Position': 'A record pattern follows instanceof or is a case label ... for (Point(var x, var y) : points), a Java 20 preview, was dropped from Java 21.' Reference 'Refused by javac 21': 'for (Point(int x, int y) : points) | a syntax error'. Together they cover both the var and the explicit-type form. Caveat: the stem names no Java version; the page frames everything as Java 21 and does not say whether later versions restored the form (its 'Later versions' box doesn't mention it), so 'in any form' is decided for Java 21 only.

recorded.prompt:q-slot-without-room:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slot-without-room:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-slot-without-room:a: Same section: the nested pattern on the null address prints false and the whole pattern fails; Summary: 'A record pattern never matches null, at any depth. A nested pattern on a component that may be null rejects the whole value'. Only var / declared-type patterns bind null, not a nested record pattern.
recorded.prompt:q-slot-without-room:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slot-without-room:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-slot-without-room:c: Same section: the pattern 'starts with an instanceof test' and the null case just prints false, no exception. The page's only NPE is after a var binding matched and the caller then called address.country(), not during matching. The page doesn't say in so many words that accessors aren't called on a null component, but the false output with no exception decides it.
recorded.prompt:q-slot-without-room:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slot-without-room:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-slot-without-room:d: Section 'Matching Calls the Accessors, and an Exception From One Arrives as MatchException': MatchException comes only when an accessor throws during a match; the null-section output shows the nested pattern yields false with no exception. Option text 'fails to take the null room apart' is partly true (the match fails), but the conclusion (throws) is refuted.
recorded.prompt:q-counter-type-changes:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-counter-type-changes:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-counter-type-changes:a: Same section and Reference table: a narrower type is a test, and a value not of the pattern's type 'doesn't match'. The page does not discuss boxing/widening between wrapper types explicitly; its only conversion remark is about primitive components ('long x and Integer x are compile errors' on an int component in Java 21), which is a different case. The test-not-cast statement plus the table is enough to refute 'converts'.
